mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of at least 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 1% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 3 consecutive months by at least 1% each month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate above 2% percentage points, combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 2%, signals aggressive monetary tightening and heightened inflation risk, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps > 2% in one month AND CPIAUCSL > 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) above trend for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which depresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS above trend for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the unemployment rate and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month, where unemployment rises while payroll employment increases, signals a shift toward lower-wage, part-time employment, which reduces labor income quality and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in real GDP (GDPC1) of at least 1% for two consecutive quarters signals a broad-based demand contraction, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.
